corrections: createProfile (backs browser.profileCreate) returns NULL (not a throw) for an invalid scope or userAgentMode enum value — 'the registry is also an IPC boundary, so runtime types alone cannot keep invalid values out of persisted metadata' per source comment, source-registry.ts:214-222. It CAN also throw: if installBrowserSessionPartitionPolicies(profile) fails, the partial session is retired (retireFailedBrowserSessionProfile) and the ORIGINAL error is rethrown (source-registry.ts:234-239) — so the RPC method browser.profileCreate's result is either {profile: BrowserSessionProfile}, {profile: null}, or a thrown/rejected error, never unconditionally successful.

deleteProfile (backs browser.profileDelete) returns false for BOTH an unknown profileId AND a profile whose scope is 'default' (protecting the default profile from deletion, source-registry.ts:263-267) — the runtime layer's {deleted, profileId} result is real, meaningful data, not a stand-in for a throw. Storage cleanup (clearStorageData/clearCache/proxy release) on the deleted partition is wrapped in its own try/catch that is fully swallowed ('cleanup is best-effort... the profile is already out of the registry', :295-297) — a real, source-confirmed partial-success shape where the profile-registry mutation always completes but the storage cleanup may silently fail.

clearDefaultSessionCookies (backs browser.profileClearDefaultCookies) wraps its entire body in try/catch and returns false on ANY failure (source-registry.ts:302-324) — so {cleared:false} is a real, reachable result, not merely a type-level possibility.

importCookiesFromBrowser (backs browser.profileImportFromBrowser's success path) dispatches to one of three fully separate family-specific importers (importCookiesFromFirefox / importCookiesFromSafari / importChromiumCookies, browser-cookie-import.ts:60-72) all returning the same discriminated union BrowserCookieImportResult = {ok:true,profileId,summary} | {ok:false,reason} (shared/browser-workspace-types.ts:215-217) — the three backend implementations were not individually opened this pass (see residualsStillOpenAfterThisRevision); their externally-visible contract is fully characterized by this shared type.

browser.clientHost.attach's registry.attach() (lease-registry.ts:106-132) throws Error('browser_host_identity_conflict') if an existing lease for the same browserHostClientId is claimed by a DIFFERENT pairedDeviceId than the caller's; otherwise runs assertBrowserHostLeaseAdmission (a further admission check, not opened line-by-line this pass but confirmed to be capable of throwing by its name and call site) before either restoring a reconnect or fencing the old lease and creating a fresh one.

browser.clientHost.commandResult's settleClientPageCommand (lease-registry.ts:259-269) requires the lease state (throws if the identity doesn't resolve to a live lease), conditionally requires the client page connection (can throw, skipped only when ledger.isUnplacedPageResult(params) is true), then delegates to ledger.settle(params) which returns a plain boolean — the RPC handler wraps this as {accepted: boolean}, confirming this is genuine pass/fail DATA, not error-signaled.

browser.clientHost.pageMetadata's updatePageMetadata (runtime-browser-page-registry.ts:108-131) throws Error('browser_page_metadata_revision_invalid') for a non-positive-integer revision, but returns FALSE (a silent no-op, not an error) when update.revision <= current.metadataRevision — an explicit, source-confirmed stale/out-of-order-update rejection distinct from any error path; the RPC handler's {accepted:boolean} result directly reflects this false case.

isExplicitContentEditableTarget/fillExplicitContentEditable (agent-browser-bridge-execution.ts:146-169), used by BOTH browser.fill and browser.clear, are STILL execAgentBrowser-based (not a fourth boundary): they probe via ['get','attr',element,'contenteditable'] then edit via ['eval','--stdin'] carrying a rich-text-edit expression through stdin rather than argv, 'to avoid argv limits and keep replacement atomic' — this corrects an ambiguity in revision 2, which did not make clear that the contentEditable path is still the same subprocess CLI boundary, just a different CLI invocation shape.

resolveMobileTouchClickPoint (agent-browser-bridge-mouse.ts:172-195), used by browser.mouseClick, is its OWN direct CDP call (dbg.sendCommand('Runtime.evaluate', ...)) separate from the mousePressed/mouseReleased dispatch that follows it — a second CDP round-trip inside one RPC method. It is gated on a positive finite radius param; ANY failure (including a non-finite radius) silently returns the fallback {x,y,adjusted:false,handled:false} rather than throwing — a genuine, source-confirmed silent-fallback design, not partial coverage.

This was WRONGLY marked 'unread, narrowly residual' in revision 2. It is fully observable and now read: every CDP 'Page.screencastFrame' event is either (a) dropped with an immediate ACK if it carries no data, (b) dropped with an ACK plus a rescheduled navigation-capture if its decoded image size doesn't match the current viewport (post-navigation host-surface leak), (c) silently dropped via a caught exception + ACK if base64 decode or size-parsing throws, or (d) queued into the frame pacer. The pacer enforces options.minFrameIntervalMs: a frame arriving within the interval is held as the single newest 'pendingFrame' (any PREVIOUS pending frame with a different sessionId is ACKed immediately, superseded frames are never emitted) and flushed by a timer; every dbg.sendCommand call (including 'Page.screencastFrameAck' itself) is wrapped in an 8000ms timeout (browser-screencast-debugger-command.ts:3,12-19) that rejects Error('Timed out while running <method>.'); if the consumer's onFrame callback signals backpressure (returns false), the frame is retried on a fixed 50ms interval (BACKPRESSURE_RETRY_MS) until accepted or the session closes/stops. The debugger attach/detach itself (electron-debugger-lease.ts) is reference-counted across concurrent callers via a Symbol-keyed owner set and only truly detaches when the last owner releases AND this lease was the one that originally attached.

timeoutClaimCorrection.priorClaim: revision 2 stated: 'tabClose's timeout-adjacent reply-error path can produce a TYPED BrowserError while its own bare timeout and tabSetProfile's bare timeout both reject a PLAIN untyped Error'

tabClose.bareTimeoutThrow: new Error('Tab close timed out') — PLAIN, untyped, unconditional
tabClose.replyErrorThrow: conditional: new BrowserError('browser_tab_not_found', reply.error) ONLY if reply.code === 'browser_tab_not_found'; new Error(reply.error) — PLAIN — for every other reply.error value

tabSetProfile.bareTimeoutThrow: new Error('Tab profile update timed out') — PLAIN, untyped, unconditional
tabSetProfile.replyErrorThrow: new Error(reply.error) — ALWAYS PLAIN; there is no reply.code field and no typed-BrowserError branch at all in this method

timeoutClaimCorrection.correctedStatement: Both methods' BARE TIMEOUT throws a plain, untyped Error — this was already true in revision 2 and remains true; it was never the disputed part. Across the four total throw sites in these two methods, exactly ONE is ever typed: tabClose's reply-error path, and only conditionally, only when the renderer's reply explicitly carries code:'browser_tab_not_found'. tabSetProfile has NO typed-error branch anywhere in its body — every failure mode it can produce (timeout, or any reply.error) is a plain Error. This is not framed as an 'inconsistency' between two symmetric round-trips; it is one method (tabClose) that added a single typed special-case for one specific renderer-reported condition, and one method (tabSetProfile) that never added that special-case at all.
